newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unisource partners want Telefonica out.
newsitem.headline: Unisource partners want Telefonica out.

text.p: Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT said on Friday that Spain's Telefonica should pull out of the Unisource telecoms joint venture.

"Following Telefonica's decision to form a strategic partnership with BT/MCI, the Unisource shareholders PTT Telecom of the Netherlands, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT, have asked Telefonica to leave their pan-European telecommunications joint venture Unisource NV," the partners said in a joint statement.

Unisource chairman Lars Berg said the partners regretted the decision but felt that Telefonica's alliance with BT/MCI was "incompatible" with its Unisource shareholding, confusing customers and slowing down the opening of the European communications market.
The statement gave no details about the legal or financial consequences of the separation, but said these were being worked out.
It said the telecoms alliance was well on track in realising its targets and would continue to develop its strategic alliance with AT&T in Europe and elsewhere.
"The Unisource shareholders are fully committed to continue to support Unisource and AT&T Unisource in growing its business aggressively," Lars Berg said.
The link-up with AT&T, formed last year, was currently being extended, Unisource said.
AT&T and Unisource Carrier Services were building the world's largest Integrated Services Digital Network to simultaneously transmit voice data and video, Unisource said.
